thesewordssluggard.title: these words
thesewordssluggard.html: See Malmesbury, Chronicle of the Kings of England book 2.10.

thesouth.title: the South
thesouth.html: Milton's margin here has: "Annal. Florent." See the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle for an entry about the accession of Ceawlin of Wessex and his successors. There is also an appended entry concerning Æthelberht of Kent. See also Deira and Flores Historiarum.

thestorygoes.title: the story
thestorygoes.html: For the story, see Bede, Ecclesiastical History of the English Nation 2.6, and in the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle under the year 616 CE.

thetenth.title: the tenth
thetenth.html: Milton's margin here has: "Sax. an. omn." See the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle: "Cerdicus, & Cynricus ejus filius cum navigiis quinque, appulerunt: in loco sc. qui Credices-ora dicitur."

thethirdhowr.title: the third howr
thethirdhowr.html: Milton's margin here has: "Sax. an. Ethelwerd." See the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle for 733 CE: "Hic Ethelbaldus castellum de Somertone obsidione cinxit: Sol autem obscurantus est." See also Æthelweard, Anglo-Saxon Chronicle.

thetown.title: the Town
thetown.html: Milton's margin here has: "Sax. an." See the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle for 913 CE. See also Hertford.

thewinter.title: The Winter
thewinter.html: Milton's margin here has: "Dion." Cassius Dio, a Roman statesman and historian, was author of Historia Romana. Milton refers to a passage in Roman History 39.53.

thewood.title: the Wood
thewood.html: Milton's margin here has: "485." See Roger of Wendover, Anglo-Saxon Chronicle: "propre Mercredes-burnan-stede."

theworse.title: the worst
theworse.html: Milton's margin here has: "Sax an." The Anglo-Saxon Chronicle records a battle at a place called "Bensintum" for 775 CE, but the Battle of Bensington occurred in 779.

theycame.title: they came
theycame.html: Milton's margin here has: "Malms. L. 1. c. 5." See Malmesbury, Chronicle of the Kings of England book 1.5. Malmesbury mistaken identifies Redwald, or Rædwald, as the first king of the East-Angles; the first was Uffa (or Uuffa, or Wuffa), according to Bede, Ecclesiastical History of the English Nation 2.15.

theycameon.title: they came on
theycameon.html: Milton's margin here has: "Sax. an." See the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle for 839 CE.

theycameto.title: they came
theycameto.html: Milton's margin here has: "Sax. ann." See the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle for 878 CE.

theyearfollowing.title: year following
theyearfollowing.html: Milton's margin here has: "698." See Bede, Ecclesiastical History of the English Nation 5.24.

theyearfollowinging.title: year following
theyearfollowinging.html: Milton's margin here has: "Sax. an. Epit. Bed. Sim. Dun." See the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle for the year 755 CE. The Chronicle is off by two years. For Bede's account, see Æthelbald's Death. See also Simeon of Durham's Historia Regum for 757 CE.

theyenterd.title: they enterd
theyenterd.html: Milton's margin here has: "Sax. an. Malms." See the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle for 938 CE. And see Malmesbury, Chronicle of the Kings of England book 2.6.

theylanded.title: they landed
theylanded.html: Milton's margin here has: "Sim. Dun." See Simeon of Durham, Historia Regum for 991 CE. See also Battle of Maldon. The Anglo-Saxon Chronicle dates the battle in 993 CE.

theytellus.title: they tell us
theytellus.html: See Geoffrey, History of the Kings of Britain 2.16 and Holinshed, Chronicle 5.21.

thirdefence.title: thir defence
thirdefence.html: Milton's margin here has: "Tacit. vit. Agric." In Tacitus's Life of Agricola 16, he accuses General Suetonius of arrogance and cruelty towards the conquered Britons. Gaius Julius Alpinus Classicianus replaced Catus Decianus as procurator of Britain in 61 CE; see Tacitus, Annals 14.38-39 for the stories of Calssicanus and Polyclitus.

thirdtime.title: third time
thirdtime.html: Milton's margin here has: "43." Presumably this indicates 43 CE. See also Claudius.

thirprey.title: thir prey
thirprey.html: Milton's margin here has: "Sax. an." See the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle for 873 CE See also Camden, "Dorset" 9.11..

thisanswer.title: this answer
thisanswer.html: Milton's margin here has: "Witichind." Milton quotes here from book 1, page 3 of the Witichindi Saxonis Rerum. Again, Camden repeats the answer in his Britannia, "English-Saxons" 2 (search for "briefly made answere").

thiseffectingulf.title: this effect
thiseffectingulf.html: The Pseudo-Ingulf's Historia is Milton's source for this story of Turketul, 495v-496r. See also Thurcytel.

thisoccasion.title: this occasion
thisoccasion.html: Milton's margin here has: "Malms." See Malmesbury, Chronicle of the Kings of England book 2.13. See also Eustace II, Count of Boulogne.

thisonly.title: this only
thisonly.html: Milton's margin here has: "Gildas." Again see Gildas, The Ruin of Britain 26.

thistime.title: this time
thistime.html: Milton's margin here has: "492." See the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle: "Andredes-ceaster."

thiswastheday.title: this was the day
thiswastheday.html: This sentence follows Tacitus very closely; see Annals 12.34.

thisyear.title: This year
thisyear.html: Milton's margin here has: "364." Valentinian was emperor of Rome from 364-375 CE. The Attacotti raided Britain from 364-368 CE.

thosecountries.title: those Countries
thosecountries.html: Milton's margin here has: "Liban. Orat. 10. Zozim. L. 3." See Libanius, Oration 10 on Julian and Zosimus, New History book 3: "As the Rhine discharges itself at the extremity of Germany into the Atlantic ocean, and the island of Britain is about nine hundred stadia from its mouths, he cut timber from the woods on the banks of the river, and built eight hundred small vessels, which he sent into Britain for a supply of corn, and brought it up the Rhine."

thosedays.title: those days
thosedays.html: Milton's margin here has: "Dion. L. 72." See Dio, Roman History 73.8.

threeotherswrite.title: Huntingdon
threeotherswrite.html: These three sources do not agree perfectly. See Huntingdon, Historia Anglorum 6, and Malmesbury, Chronicle of the Kings of England book 2.11, and the Flores Historiarum for 1017 CE.

threesons.title: three Sons
threesons.html: Milton's margin here has: "Sax. an. Ethelw. Florent." See the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle: "Hic venit Ella Britanniam, & tres filii sui. Cymen, Wlentingus [Þencing], & Cissa." See also Æthelweard, Anglo-Saxon Chronicle page 7: "Aldredes-Leage." And see Flores Historiarum page 38: "Plenting."

threeyears2.title: 3 years
threeyears2.html: Milton's margin here has: "Malms." See Malmesbury, Chronicle of the Kings of England book 1.1. See also Eormenric of Kent.

thrownoverthem.title: thrown over them
thrownoverthem.html: See Gildas, The Ruin of Britain 28. See also Mordred.

thusrelated.title: thus related
thusrelated.html: As found in Bede, Ecclesiastical History of the English Nation 2.12.

tideorweather.title: round about the Coast
tideorweather.html: Milton's margin here has: "Dion. L. 66." See Dio, Roman History 66.20. Tacitus says the rebels sailed around Britain (Life of Agricola 28).

tillhistime.title: till his time
tillhistime.html: Milton's margin here has: "Mat. West." See the Flores Historiarum. Milton's negative take on Lent does not come from Bede. See also Eorcenberht of Kent.

timorouscaptain.title: timorous Captain
timorouscaptain.html: See Florence, Chronicron ex Chronicis. See also Ralph the Timid.

toadore.title: to adore
toadore.html: Milton's margin here has: "627." Bede gives this as the date of Edwin's baptism: Ecclesiastical History of the English Nation 2.14. Milton may be confusing Eadfrid as "Eanfrid," but see Bede, 2.20: "Edwin was killed on the 12th of October, in the year of our Lord 633, being then forty-seven years of age, and all his army was either slain or dispersed. In the same war also, before him, fell Osfrid, one of his sons, a warlike youth; Eanfrid, another of them, compelled by necessity, went over to King Penda."

toald.title: toald
toald.html: OED: "To attract, entice, allure, decoy; to incite, instigate."

toassist.title: to assist
toassist.html: Milton's margin here has: "Sax. an." See the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle for 945 CE.

tobeslain.title: to be slain
tobeslain.html: Milton's margin here has: "Sim. Dun." See Simeon of Durham's Historia Regum for 778 CE.

tobetray.title: to betray
tobetray.html: Milton's margin here has: "Malmsb. L. 1 c. 3." See Malmesbury, Chronicle of the Kings of England book 1.3.

tofallinto.title: to fall into
tofallinto.html: Milton's margin here has: "Sax. ann." See the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle for 905 CE See also Cricklade in Wiltshire.

toflight.title: to flight
toflight.html: Milton's margin here has: "556." See the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle : "Beran byrig;" Milton's "Beranvirig" may well be a misprint.

toforsakeit.title: to forsake it
toforsakeit.html: See Bede, Ecclesiastical History of the English Nation 3.22.

togather.title: to gather
togather.html: Milton's margin here has: "Sim. Dun." See Simeon, Historia Regum for 1041 CE. A housecarl is a member of the bodyguard of a Danish or English king or noble.

togodumnus.title: Togodumnus
togodumnus.html: These names come from Camden, "Essex" 16.

tohaveslain.title: to have slain
tohaveslain.html: Milton's margin here has: "Sim. Dun." See Simeon of Durham, Historia Regum for 952 CE. See also Wulfstan.

toincrease.title: to increase
toincrease.html: Milton's margin here has: "604." See Bede, Ecclesiastical History of the English Nation 5.epitome: "In the year 604, the East Saxons received the faith of Christ, under King Sabert, and Bishop Mellitus."

toinsertit.title: to insert it
toinsertit.html: The Battle of Badon Hill is notoriously difficult to date precisely; so much of the legendary Arthur surrounds accounts of it.

tointimat.title: new league and amity
tointimat.html: Milton's margin here has: "Nennius." See Nennius, Historia Brittonum 45-46: "with insidious intention they sent messengers to the king, with offers of peace and perpetual friendship; unsuspicious of treachery, the monarch, after advising with his elders, accepted the proposals."

toldof.title: Told of
toldof.html: Milton's margin here has: "Huntingd." See Huntingdon, Historia Anglorum 6. See also Malcolm III of Scotland.

tolearn.title: to learn
tolearn.html: Milton's margin here has: "Cæsar Com. L. 4." See Commentaries 4.20. Caesar mentions the Druids of Gaul in Commentaries 6.13-14.

tookbystorm.title: took by storm
tookbystorm.html: Milton's margin here has: "Sim. Dun." See Simeon of Durham, Historia Regum for 993 CE. Bamburgh is about 58 miles from Durham.

tookfromthepyrats.title: then much infested
tookfromthepyrats.html: Milton's margin here has: "285." Maximian's campaign in Gaul against rebellious tribes was in 286 CE.

tookpossession.title: took possession
tookpossession.html: Milton's margin here has: "Sim. Dun." See Simeon of Durham's Historia Regum for 914, 919, 920 CE. See also Sitric Cáech.

tookthecastle.title: took the castle
tookthecastle.html: Milton's margin here has: "Huntingd. Camd." See Huntingdon, Historia Anglorum 5, and Camden, "Wales" 23.5.

tookthefield.title: took the Field
tookthefield.html: Milton's margin here has: "81." Agricola's advance to the Firth of Tay took place in the summer of 79 CE, which would have been his third summer in Britain.

tookthegovernment.title: took the Government
tookthegovernment.html: Milton's margin here has: "Capitolin. in Alb." See Augustan History, "Life of Clodius Albinus" 3.5; the oration Milton refers to starts at 13.5 Clodius Albinus was proclaimed emperor by the legions in Britain and Hispania in 193 CE.

tooktowife.title: took to Wife
tooktowife.html: Milton's margin here has: "Asser." See Asser, Life of Alfred.

topromise.title: to promise
topromise.html: Milton's margin here has: "Malms." See Malmesbury, Chronicle of the Kings of England book 2.13. See also Edith of Wessex.

toreign.title: to reign
toreign.html: Milton's margin here has: "614." See the Flores Historiarum.

torepressswedes.title: to repress
torepressswedes.html: See Huntingdon, Historia Anglorum 6, and the Flores Historiarum for 1024 CE.

tosettle.title: to settle
tosettle.html: Milton's margin here has: "Sigon." See Sigonius, Historiarum de occidentali imperio pages 38-39.

tosucceed.title: succeed him
tosucceed.html: Milton's margin here has: "Malms. Sax an." See Malmesbury, Chronicle of the Kings of England book 1.2 and the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle .

totalloss.title: Wippeds-fleot
totalloss.html: Milton's margin here has: "465." The Anglo-Saxon Chronicle calls the place "Wyþþedes-Fleot."

totness.title: Totness
totness.html: Totnes, a town at the head of the Dart River estuary in Devon.

tovisit.title: to visit
tovisit.html: Milton's margin here has: "Sim. Dun." See Simeon, Historia Regum for 1059 CE.

traditionalbeginning.title: Traditional Beginning
traditionalbeginning.html: That is, the earliest traditional stories of Britain's beginnings which, Milton acknowledges below, may be largely fictional and yet contain "reliques of somthing true."

traytoredric.title: Edric of Streon
traytoredric.html: See Eadric Streona; Milton's Edric of Streon is probably a mistake.

treasonofhiswife.title: Treason of his Wife
treasonofhiswife.html: Milton's margin here has: "Sax. an." The Anglo-Saxon Chronicle has no record at all for the year 659.

trebellius.title: Trebellius Maximus
trebellius.html: Marcus Trebellius Maximus was appointed governor of Britain in 63 CE.

trebonius.title: Trebonius
trebonius.html: Gaius Trebonius was made one of Caesar's legates in 54 CE. He was later among those who plotted Caesar's assassination. See also Caesar, Commentaries 5.17.

trinobantes.title: Trinobantes
trinobantes.html: The Trinobantes or Trinovantes were a Celtic tribe of pre-Roman Britain. See Caesar, Commentaries 5.20.

trinovant.title: Trinovant
trinovant.html: The earliest name of London, also Trinovantum.

troublesometimes.title: troublesome times
troublesometimes.html: Milton's margin here has: "193." Septimus Severus was proclaimed emperor by the Roman troops in 193 CE, but Didius Julianus also made a claim to the imperial throne; civil war ensued.

truerstories.title: truer stories
truerstories.html: Probably Milton refers to Gildas, The Ruin of Britain 23: "that proud tyrant Gurthrigern [Vortigern]."

trutulensis.title: Trutulensis
trutulensis.html: Trutulensis Portus was the Roman name for "a harbour on the northeastern coast of Britain, near the estuary Taüs (Tay)."

tucks.title: Tucks
tucks.html: A tuck is "a sword; esp. a broadsword" (OED). A "piked" target is a shield with a spike on it.

turbulent.title: turbulent
turbulent.html: Milton's margin here has: "Tacit. an. 12." Milton follows Tacitus's Annals 14.31-40 from this point until the death of Aulus Didius Gallus.

turnspriest.title: turns Priest
turnspriest.html: Sozomenus, in Ecclesiastical History 9.15: "Constantine throws aside the Emblems of Imperial Power, and is ordained as Presbyter." Also, "Constantine, with his son Julian, was sent into Italy, but he was waylaid and killed."

twiceking.title: twice King
twiceking.html: Milton's margin here has: "Sim. Dun." See Simeon of Durham's Historia Regum for 796 CE. See also the entry for 799 which says Osbald died an abbot.

twocomets.title: two Comets
twocomets.html: Milton's margin here has: "728." See Bede, Ecclesiastical History of the English Nation 5.23: "In the year of our Lord's incarnation 729, two comets appeared about the sun, to the great terror of the beholders." and 5.24: "In the year 729, comets appeared; the holy Egbert departed; and Osric died."

twodeputies.title: two Deputies
twodeputies.html: Milton's margin here has: "Digest. L. 28. tit. 6." See the Corpus Juris Civilis, Digesta 28.6.2.4: "Quae sententia rescripto imperatoris nostri ad virium lupum [Virius Lupus] Brittanniae praesidem comprobata est." Virius Lupus was appointed governor of Britain in 197 CE, and served, mostly in Caledonia against the Maeatae confederation, until 201 or 202; Sextus Varius Marcellus may have been sent by Severus to help him govern. See also Camden, "Romans in Britaine" 66.

twomonasteries.title: built two monasteries
twomonasteries.html: See the Flores Historiarum for 939 CE. See also Milton, Dorset.

twonoblemen.title: two Noblemen
twonoblemen.html: Milton's margin here has: "Sim. Dun." See Simeon of Durham's Historia Regum for 780 CE. See also "Osbald" in the DNB. Seletune is probably Nether Silton, in the North Riding of Yorkshire.

ulpius.title: Ulpius Marcellus
ulpius.html: Ulpius Marcellus is recorded as governor of Roman Britain in an inscription of 176-80 CE.

understood.title: understood
understood.html: Milton's margin here has: "Sim. Dun." See Simeon of Durham, Historia Regum for 1002 CE.

uninfested.title: uninfested
uninfested.html: Milton's margin here has: "Hoved." See Roger of Hovedon, Chronica for 980-988 CE.

uninhabited.title: uninhabited
uninhabited.html: Milton's margin here has: "Bed. L. 1. c. 15." See Bede, Ecclesiastical History of the English Nation 1.15: "the country which is called Anglia, and which is said, from that time, to remain desert to this day."

unitedforces.title: united Forces
unitedforces.html: Milton's margin here has: "Camden." See Camden, "Wales" 24.3. See also Battle of Buttington.

unnatural.title: unnatural and disloyal
unnatural.html: Milton's margin here has: "Asser. Malms. Sim. Dun." See Asser, Life of Alfred, Malmesbury, Chronicle of the Kings of England book 2.3, and Simeon of Durham's Historia Regum for 855 CE.. See also Æthelbald, King of Wessex.

unnaturallust.title: unnaturall lust
unnaturallust.html: In Aaron Thompson's translation of Geoffrey, we read, "addicted himself to sodomy, preferring unnatural lust to the pleasures of the conjugal state" (History of the Kings of Britain 2.6).

unsentfor.title: the same
unsentfor.html: Milton's margin here has: "Calvisius." Sethus Calvisius's Opus Chronologicum identifies Normans as originally Danes.

unsettledness.title: unsettl'dness
unsettledness.html: Milton's margin here has: "Dion. L. 53.24" See Dio's Roman History 53.22.

upanddown.title: up and down
upanddown.html: Milton's margin here has: "679." See the Flores Historiarum. See also Wilfrid.

uponkent.title: upon Kent
uponkent.html: Milton's margin here has: "Sim. Dun." See Simeon of Durham, Historia Regum for 999 CE.

upontheneck.title: upon the neck
upontheneck.html: OED: "on the top of; immediately upon or after(wards)."

usipian.title: Germans
usipian.html: Tacitus speaks of a "Usipian chort" in Life of Agricola 28.

usurpingthechair.title: usurping the Chair
usurpingthechair.html: See Gildas, The Ruin of Britain 66: "being careful with their whole hearts to fulfil their own lustful desires, some of them usurping with unclean feet the seat of the apostle Peter; but for the demerit of their covetousness falling down into the pestilent chair of the traitor Judas."

valentia.title: Valentia
valentia.html: Land of Valens may have been a Roman Province in Britain. See also Londinium : "The city seems to have been the seat of the diocesan vicar and one of the provincial governors following the Diocletian Reforms around the year 300; it had been renamed Augusta—a common epithet of provincial capitals—by 368."

venutius.title: Venutius
venutius.html: Venutius was a first-century king of the Brigantes. Most of the following story of Venutius and Cartimandua comes from Tacitus, Annals 12.40 and Histories 3.45

veranius.title: Verannius
veranius.html: Quintus Veranius Nepos was made governor of Britain in 57 CE. Milton now turns to Tacitus, Annals 14.29-39 for the careers of Veranius and Gaius Suetonius Paulinus.

verulam.title: Verulam
verulam.html: Also known as Verulamium, an ancient Roman town near what is now St. Albans in Hertfordshire. See Camden's comments in "Hertfordshire" 9.

vices.title: ignoble vices
vices.html: Milton's margin here has: "Florent. Sim. Dun." See Flores Historiarum, and Simeon of Durham, Historia Regum.

videna.title: Videna
videna.html: See Geoffery, History of the Kings of Britain 2.16.

vigenius.title: Vigenius, and Peredure
vigenius.html: Sometimes also called Ingenius and Peredurus; see Geoffrey, History of the Kings of Britain 3.18.

violenthands.title: Osred
violenthands.html: Milton's margin here has: "Malms." See Malmesbury, Chronicle of the Kings of England book 1.3.

virunnius.title: Virunnius
virunnius.html: Ludovicus Ponticus Virunnius was the author of Britannicæ historiæ libri 6.

visagegrim.title: visage grim
visagegrim.html: Milton's margin here has: "Dion." Dio reports that Boudica fell sick and died (Roman History 62.12); Tacitus reports the suicide by poison story (Annals 14.37) and the casualty figures.

visithim.title: visit him
visithim.html: Milton's margin here has: "Malms." See Malmesbury, Chronicle of the Kings of England book 2.10.

vortigernian.title: Guorthigirniaun
vortigernian.html: Vortigern was said to have taken refuge in north Wales, but the River Teifi (Milton's Tiebi) is in western Wales.

vortipor.title: Vortipor
vortipor.html: See Gildas, The Ruin of Britain 31. See also Vortiporius.

wantondeeds.title: wanton deeds
wantondeeds.html: See Bede, Ecclesiastical History of the English Nation 4.25.

warlikematters.title: warlike matters
warlikematters.html: Milton's margin here has: "Pontan. L. 4." See Pontanus, Rerum Danicarum Historia book 4.

warrdonanna.title: warr'd on Anna
warrdonanna.html: Milton's margin here has: "Sax. an." The Anglo-Saxon Chronicle records the death of Anna in the year 654 CE. Bede, in Ecclesiastical History of the English Nation 3.18, claims that Peada slew Anna.

warring.title: oft-times warring
warring.html: Milton's margin here has: "Mela." See The Situation of the World (translated by Arthur Golding 1585) 78-79.

wasburied.title: was buried
wasburied.html: Milton's margin here has: "Sax. an." See the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle for 836 CE Ecgberht of Wessex probably died in 839 CE.

wasburiedat.title: was buried
wasburiedat.html: Milton's margin here has: "Florent." See the Flores Historiarum for 1035 CE.

wasburiedatwin.title: was buried
wasburiedatwin.html: Milton's margin here has: "Sim. Dun." See Simeon, Historia Regum for 1052 CE.

wasburnt.title: was burnt
wasburnt.html: Milton's margin here has: "769." Catterick is in North Yorkshire.

wasfought.title: was fought
wasfought.html: Milton's margin here has: "Florent. Huntingd." See the Flores Historiarum page 39: "Mercredesburne." See also Huntingdon, Historia Anglorum 2.8.

wasgone.title: was gone
wasgone.html: Milton's margin here has: "Sim. Dun." See Simeon, Historia Regum for 1061 CE.

wasprecedent.title: 8 years
wasprecedent.html: Milton's margin here has: "642." See Bede, Ecclesiastical History of the English Nation 3.9 who reports that Oswald reigned for "nine years."

wastroubld.title: not in his power
wastroubld.html: Milton's margin here has: "617." See Bede, Ecclesiastical History of the English Nation 2.6.

watchword.title: heated with Wine
watchword.html: Milton's margin here has: "Malms." See Malmesbury, Chronicle of the Kings of England book 1.1, pages 11-12.

weariedout.title: wearied out
weariedout.html: Milton's margin here has: "Sim. Dun." See Simeon of Durham, Historia Regum for 1007 CE. The marriage to Edgitha is not mentioned until the entry for 1009.

welcome.title: Ordovices
welcome.html: The Ordovices, says Tacitus, "destroyed nearly the whole of a squadron of allied cavalry" (Life of Agricola 18).

wellunderstanding.title: understanding
wellunderstanding.html: Milton's margin here has: "Eadmer. Florent." Eadmer was an English historian, theologian, and ecclesiastic of the 11th and early 12th centuries. His Historia novorum in Anglia was edited by John Selden and published in London in 1623. Eadmer opens book I of his history with an account of Danish invasions during the reign of Æthelred. See also Flores Historiarum for 980 and 982 CE.

westernprovinces.title: Western Provinces
westernprovinces.html: Milton's margin here has: "Vopisc. in Carin." see "Lives of Carus, Carinus, and Numerian" 16-18.

westrelates.title: relates
westrelates.html: See the Flores Historiarum for 1016 CE.

whatremaind.title: what remain'd
whatremaind.html: Milton's margin here has: "Mat. West." See the Flores Historiarum.

whichtime.title: which time
whichtime.html: Milton's margin here has: "Constant. Bede." Constantius of Lyons, in his Life of Germanus 2.1-4, tells of a second visit to Britain by Germanus, acccompanied by Severus. See also Bede, Ecclesiastical History of the English Nation 1.21.

wholearmy.title: whole Army
wholearmy.html: Milton's margin here has: "Bed. l. 2. c. 3. Malms. Florent. Sax. an." See Bede, Ecclesiastical History of the English Nation 2.5 (not chapter 3). See also See Malmesbury, Chronicle of the Kings of England book 1.2.

wholenation.title: Levermaur
wholenation.html: Milton's margin here has: "Nennius." Nennius, in his Historia Brittonum 22, only says "After the birth of Christ, one hundred and sixty-seven years, King Lucius, with all the chiefs of the British people, received baptism, in consequence of a legation sent by the Roman emperors and pope Evaristus." But Camden attributes the origin of surname Lever Maur ("Prince of great glory") to "Ninnius" ("Romans in Britaine" 64).

whomadepeace.title: who made peace
whomadepeace.html: Milton's margin here has: "Calvis." Sethus Calvisius's Opus Chronologicum cites Malmesbury's account of the letter, but dates it 990 CE.

whosename.title: whose name
whosename.html: Milton's margin here has: "Camd." See Camden's Britannia, "Romans in Britaine" 4. 70. Ulpius Cornelius Laelianus rebelled against Posthumus in 269 CE.

wibbandum.title: Wibbandum
wibbandum.html: The Battle of Wibbandum was joined by Ceawlin and Cutha against Æthelberht of Kent in 568 CE according to the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle.

wickedly.title: wickedly
wickedly.html: Milton's margin here has: "Malms." Malmesbury (Chronicle of the Kings of England book 2.10) and the Flores Historiarum date the succession 979 CE.

wickedwoman.title: every way wicked
wickedwoman.html: Milton's margin here has: "Malms. L. 2. Asser." See Malmesbury, Chronicle of the Kings of England book 2.2 and Asser, Life of Alfred. See also Eadburh.

winburne.title: Winburne
winburne.html: See Camden, "Dorset" 9.11. See also Wimborne Minster.

wineandale.title: Wine and Ale
wineandale.html: See Roger of Hoveden's Annals: "Through the influence of this king, after he had become a monk, licence was granted to the monks of the church of Lindisfarne to drink wine or ale; for before, they were in the habit of drinking only milk or water."

winterdagainagain.title: winterd again
winterdagainagain.html: Milton's margin here has: "Sax. an." See the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle for 854 CE.

wisestman.title: wisest man
wisestman.html: Without naming any source, French Fogle, the Yale Prose editor, identifies this wisest man as Illtud, "virtual founder of Welsh Christianity" (Volume 5 part 1.178n.35).

wisheshim.title: wishes him
wisheshim.html: See Gildas, The Ruin of Britain 30. See also Aurelius Conanus.

with12men.title: with 12 men
with12men.html: Milton's margin here has: "Sax. an. Malms." See the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle for 686 CE. See also Malmesbury, Chronicle of the Kings of England 1.1.

with23.title: coming with 23
with23.html: Milton's margin here has: "Sim. Dun." See Simeon of Durham's Historia Regum for 877 CE. See also the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle for 878 CE.

withaditch.title: with a Ditch
withaditch.html: Milton's margin here has: "Cæsar." See Caesar's Commentaries 5.9 and 5.21.

withallspeed.title: with all speed
withallspeed.html: Milton's margin here has: "Florent. Sim. Dun." See the Flores Historiarum for 1016 CE: "quinti idus Junii," not May as Milton has it. See also Simeon of Durham, Historia Regum for 1016 CE, and Siege of London.

withanavy.title: with a Navy
withanavy.html: Milton's margin here has: "Malms. Mathew Paris." See Malmesbury, Chronicle of the Kings of England book 2.13. See also Matthew Paris, Chronica maiora 2:"regem Norwagiae cum mille navibus" and Harald Hardrada.

withhisarmy.title: with his Army
withhisarmy.html: Milton's margin here has: "Sax. an." See the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle for 919 CE.

withhisfather.title: with his Father
withhisfather.html: Milton's margin here has: "Zozim. L. 4, Sigon." See Zosimus, New History book 4: "He was offended that Theodosius should be thought worthy of being made emperor, while he himself had no honourable employment. He therefore cherished the animosity of the soldiers towards the emperor. They were thus easily induced to revolt and to declare Maximus emperor." See also Sigonius, Historiarum de occidentali imperio page 170.

withhisnobles.title: with his Noble
withhisnobles.html: Milton's margin here has: "716." See the details of Boniface's letter in Malmesbury, Chronicle of the Kings of England book 1.4.

withinayear.title: within a year
withinayear.html: Milton's margin here has: "755." See the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle for the year 755 CE (see also a translation). This long narrative of the career of Cynewulf of Wessex described events that took place much later, in 786 CE. (Blair 210).

withinthreeyears.title: within three years
withinthreeyears.html: Milton's margin here has: "658." See Bede, Ecclesiastical History of the English Nation 3.24.

withiron.title: could not gain
withiron.html: See Malmesbury, Chronicle of the Kings of England book 2.10: Archbishop Siric "advised that money should repel those whom the sword could not."

withmuchwisdom.title: with much wisdom
withmuchwisdom.html: Milton's margin here has: "Zozim. l. 1." Zosimus the Historian, in his New History book 1, reports that "Victorinus, a Moor" helped Probus quash a rebellion led by Saturnius, also a Moor.

withoutissue.title: without issue
withoutissue.html: Milton's margin here has: "Geff. Mon." See Geoffrey, History of the Kings of Britain 5.1.

withoutjustcause.title: without just cause
withoutjustcause.html: Milton's margin here has: "759." See Simeon of Durham's Historia Regum for 758 CE and 759 CE. The Anglo-Saxon Chronicle records Æthelberht's death under the year 760; the correct date is 762 CE.

withspoils.title: with spoils
withspoils.html: Milton's margin here has: "Sim. Dun." See Simeon of Durham, Historia Regum for 949-950 CE.

withthecitizens.title: with the Citizens
withthecitizens.html: Milton's margin here has: "Aelred in the life of Ed. Conf." See Aelred of Rievaulx, and his Life of Saint Edward the Confessor 5r.

withvictories.title: with victories
withvictories.html: See Tacitus, Life of Agricola 5 and 7-8 for accounts of Agricola's experience in British wars.

witnessing.title: witnessing
witnessing.html: See Gildas, The Ruin of Britain 26: "our foreign wars having ceased, but our civil troubles still remaining."

wodensbeorth.title: Wodens Beorth
wodensbeorth.html: Milton's margin here has: "592." The Flores Historiarum sets the defeat of Ceaulinus (Milton's Keaulin) and the accession of Ceolricus (Coelric) at 593 CE.

wondrousfair.title: Virgin wondrous fair
wondrousfair.html: Milton's margin here has: "Nenn." See Nennius, Historia Brittonum 37-38 (search for "enjoined his daughter to serve them "). Geoffrey of Monmouth calls her Rowen: History of the Kings of Britain 6.12. See also Rowena.

wonhimhatred.title: won him hatred
wonhimhatred.html: Milton's margin here has: "Dion. L. 66." See Dio, Roman History 66.20.

wordforword.title: word for word
wordforword.html: Henry of Huntingdon offers a Latin version of the Old English poem, though certainly not "word for word" as Milton supposes. See Huntingdon, Historia Anglorum 5.

writersaffirm.title: Writers affirm
writersaffirm.html: See George Buchanan, History of Scotland 5.15: "As touching Eugenius, the King of the Scots, there goes a double report of him. Some say he was slain in fight beyond the River Humber; others that he died a natural death."

wroughthispeace.title: wrought his peace
wroughthispeace.html: Milton's margin here has: "Mat. West." See the Flores Historiarum for 1049 CE.

year547.title: year 547
year547.html: Milton's margin here has: "547." See the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle for the genealogy of the Northumbrian royal line.

year571.title: year 571
year571.html: Milton's margin here has: "Malms. L. 1. c. 6." See Malmesbury, Chronicle of the Kings of England book 1.6. See also Tytila of East Anglia.

year633.title: year 633
year633.html: Milton's margin here has: "633." Bede, Ecclesiastical History of the English Nation 2.20. See also Cadwallon ap Cadfan and Penda of Mercia.

year640.title: year 640
year640.html: Milton's margin here has: "640." The Anglo-Saxon Chronicle for the year 640 CE erroneously reports "Redbaldus"as King of Kent instead of Eadbald who died that year; Rædwald is considered to have died in around 624 CE. See also Bede, Ecclesiastical History of the English Nation 3.8.

year749.title: the year 749
year749.html: See Simeon of Durham's Historia Regum for 749 CE.

yearafterwhich.title: year after which
yearafterwhich.html: Milton's margin here has: "Sim. Dun." See Simeon of Durham's Historia Regum for 765 and 769 CE.

yearensueing.title: Now
yearensueing.html: Milton's margin here has: "Hoved. Malms." See Roger of Hoveden's Annals: "In the year 744, a battle was fought between the Picts and the Britons; and in the following year, fiery strokes were beheld in the air, such as no men of that generation had ever seen before, and were visible throughout almost all the night of the calends of January." See also Malmesbury's list of East Saxon Kings in Chronicle of the Kings of England book 1.6.

yearfollowing.title: year following
yearfollowing.html: Milton's margin here has: "Sax. an." See the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle for 716 CE.

yearlanding.title: next year landing
yearlanding.html: Milton's margin here has: "Sim. Dun." See Simeon of Durham, Historia Regum for 1004 CE. See also Ulfcytel Snillingr.

yetreignd.title: yet reign'd
yetreignd.html: Milton's margin here has: "360." Scots and Picts raided the British in 360 CE.
